AnswerMeta.description:
`_meta.acpmux` on an answer. Every field is optional; a relayed allow
carries the decision proof, the person's app may say whose answer it
relays, and a peer forwarding for its Web client says `via: "web"`.

answeredBy.description: `{device, feedItem}`, from the person's connection only.

approverDecision.description:
An enrolled approver's signed answer beside `decisionNonce`: a phone's
(`hub/approvers.rs`) or a Mac's (`hub/mac_approvers.rs`).

approverDecisions.description:
A group's one-time allow from an enrolled Mac (`_acpmux/permission_group_respond`):
one signed allow per pending member of the group, by permission id.

ApproverDecision.description:
`{approver, expiresAt, signature}`: ECDSA P-256 / SHA-256, raw `r || s` as
lowercase hex, over the approver's message for this exact answer.

afterSeq.description: Page forward from here (oldest first) when `beforeSeq` is absent.

beforeSeq.description: The newest `limit` records before this one.

eventStream.description:
Send every matching record as `_acpmux/event`; else the agent's
updates arrive as ACP `session/update` and acpmux's own as
`_acpmux/event`.

visible.description: False attaches without showing the chat (`hub/seen.rs`); default true.

waitLogs.description: Wait for restart-time log restoration before answering; false serves the page immediately.

hasMore.description: More records lie beyond this page.

pageThrough.description:
How far the page holds: every record of the kinds asked from the page's first one up to it
is in the page (a peer's copy of the chat, `hub/peer_snapshot.rs`, covers that far). The
log's last seq, read before the page, for the newest page; a page of older records
(`beforeSeq`) or a forward one with more to read holds only to its own last record.

presence.description: Who has the chat open now, this attachment included (`hub/presence.rs`).

turnOpener.description:
The prompt that opened the turn the page starts inside, when the page starts inside one
with older records before it (`server/requests/turn_opener.rs`); null otherwise. An older
acpmux leaves it out, and its client reads it with `_acpmux/events`.

Author.description:
The person a request comes from (`hub/author.rs`): stamped by the daemon that admitted
them, and accepted only from the unix socket or a peer forwarding for its own.

approval.description: A link guest's prompts wait for the chat owner's approval.

id.description: `tailnet:<login>` until accounts are mapped, then `user_…`; one line of at most 256 bytes.

AuthorMetaFields.description: `_meta.acpmux` of a request that may name its person; other fields pass.

Autocompact.description: Whether a harness's autocompact is capped (`UsageStats.autocompact`).

oneOf.description: A flag, env or setting caps it.
Nothing caps it: the harness's own default applies.
Not known: its argv is not this daemon's, or a value or file it reads could not be read.

Carrier.description: The carrier a live link runs over (`carrier`); null while no link is open.

oneOf.description: Straight to the peer: its WebSocket URL, or the paired machines' WireGuard link.
An `ssh -W` tunnel to the peer's daemon.
Relayed by the team hub. Not sent by acpmux yet (carrier slice 3).
cmux Cloud's relay. Not sent by acpmux yet (carrier slice 3).

CreatedBy.description:
Who created a session (`hub/created_by.rs`), the shape cmux-tui's
`workspace.create {created_by}` takes.

session.description: The acpmux session whose agent created it; only for `agent`.

workspace.description:
The cmux workspace it was created from (lowercase UUID): the agent session's
workspace for an agent, else the one the create named.

oneOf.description: This host's app, or a connection that proved it is the person.

An agent session: its shell's `acpmux new` (a proven caller token) or its
`start_session` tool.
Any other client: a script or the CLI outside a chat.

Done.description: An acknowledgement with nothing in it.

DownCause.description:
Why a link is down (`cause`), so a surface can tell this Mac's network apart from the
machine. Null while the link is up or on its way the first time.

oneOf.description:
This machine's own network is down: the last attempt failed before it left this host
(no route, no DNS).

The team hub does not answer, so a relayed link cannot be made. Not sent yet: it needs
the hub carrier's probe (carrier slice 3).
This machine's network works, and the peer (or its daemon) does not answer.
The peer refused this daemon's token.

Enforcement.description: What limits the session's agent as far as acpmux can tell.

policy.description:
The acpmux permission policy (the session's own, else the daemon
default), or `unknown`.

ErrorDetails.description: The facts of a typed failure (`errorKind`); only the keys that apply are present.

binary.description: The program that could not start.

path.description: The folder whose disk is full or low.

peer.description: The peer, by its name in `acpmux host ls`.

queued.description: The message is held in the durable outbox and goes when the peer or daemon is back.

EventKinds.description:
Which records a page or an event stream carries: one kind, or any of
several. Absent or null: every record.

afterSeq.description: Records after this one; it may not lie beyond the last record.

beforeSeq.description: The newest `limit` records before this one.

promptIndex.description:
Every prompt before `beforeSeq`, oldest first, each cut to its id and the start of its text,
in one reply (`Hub::prompt_index`): `kinds`, `limit` and `maxBytes` are not read.

subagent.description:
Only this subagent's own records: the updates acpmux tagged with it and those that start
or change it (`EventFilter::of_subagent`). A subagent pane reads its subagent with it.

createdAt.description:
The session the page is of (its `createdAt`): a session recreated under the same id while
the page was asked is another journal (`hub/peer_snapshot.rs`).

pageThrough.description:
How far the page holds: every record of the kinds asked after `afterSeq` up to it is in the
page (`hub/peer_snapshot.rs`). The log's last seq, read before the page, when the page reads
to its end; else (`beforeSeq`, or `hasMore`) the page's own last record.

ForkParams.description:
`acp.session.fork`: a completed-turn, live, or before-prompt fork.
Before-prompt requests require requestId and omit both throughSeq and live.

beforePromptId.description: Recorded prompt identity, nonempty and at most 512 UTF-8 bytes. Claude/Codex only.

cancelToken.description:
The caller's name for this fork while it is made, at most 128 bytes: `_acpmux/kill` with
`cancelFork` and this token stops it, or takes it back once made (`hub/fork_cancel.rs`).

requestId.description: Persisted retry identity, nonempty and at most 512 UTF-8 bytes; scoped to the source.

Lane.description: The session's lane (cx-v9k2f), decided once by the daemon (`views::lane`).

error.description: The failed or lost turn's error text, secrets masked (`secret_scan`).

since.description: Unix ms the state began; null when the daemon does not know.

stalledSince.description:
A `working` lane that has stalled: since when its turn has had no tool
call in flight and no sign of its model (`turn.stalledSince`); null
otherwise. The state stays `working`, so a client that reads only it
is unchanged.

step.description:
What the session is doing now, one line: the running turn's prompt,
else the agent's last reply line, secrets masked (`secret_scan`).

title.description:
The session's title, else its latest prompt, one line, secrets masked
(`secret_scan`).

LastReturn.description:
A person's return to a chat that kept working (`hub/seen.rs`): the log seq they had seen when
they left, and how many turns ended while nobody showed it.

LastTurn.description:
The outcome of the session's last turn. Keys the turn result lacked
are absent.

detail.description: Why a turn ended without an answer, e.g. `outcome_unknown`.

errorKind.description:
What kind of failure a failed turn was (`recovery.rs`): `disk.full`, `disk.low`,
`peer.unreachable`, `daemon.restarting`, `spawn.failed`, `agent.exited`,
`auth.signed_out` or `auth.expired`. A client treats a kind it does not know as a plain
error. The same key is on a request's error `data` and on the `turn_error` and
`turn_result` records.

recovery.description: One sentence saying what to do about the failure.

LifecycleReceipt.description:
A durable lifecycle fact supplied by an explicit producer. This contract
is intentionally optional and opaque to the session sidebar until a
producer wires it to a real controller receipt.

LoopEpisodeSummary.description:
The bounded diagnosis shown beside a looping chat. The daemon emits one event when this
becomes active and another when progress clears it; the summary lets a newly attached client
render the current state without replaying the transcript.

MachineLink.description: A machine link's whole state (`link`): what every surface draws, from acpmux alone.

oneOf.description: The handshake finished and the peer answers.
Not reached yet, this run or a saved one; the first attempt runs.

Down after it was reached; its last-known sessions stay listed. Attempts go on
(`nextRetryAt`).
The peer's daemon announced a restart (an update); it is dialed again at once.
The WebSocket is open and the handshake runs, or a ping went unanswered: slow, not gone.
Never reached and attempts failed, or removed. Attempts go on (`nextRetryAt`).
The peer refused this daemon's token (HTTP 401 or 403): a person must sign in again.

The peer is too old to link with: a person must update it. Not sent by acpmux yet; a
renderer draws it when a carrier reports it.

A Cloud machine that is paused; it resumes on use. Not sent by acpmux yet (the Cloud
carrier does not carry acpmux until carrier slice 3); a renderer draws it when sent.

recipient.description: Session recipient for ordinary mail. Omit when `target` is supplied.

target.description: Quiet reports alias (`reports:<person>`). Omit for session mail.

McpServerStatus.description: `failed` also for one that waits on a sign-in (Claude Code `needs-auth`).

McpServerSummary.description: One MCP server a harness loaded (`SessionSummary::mcp_servers`).

MemberApproverDecision.description: One group member's signed one-time allow: the member prompt's nonce and the signature.

MessageEvent.description: The sender and receiver projection of a persisted session-to-session message.

Participant.description:
One person in a chat. The hub never marks the caller's own entry: a connection may carry
several people, so the client compares ids (a caller with no author is `owner`).

devices.description: How many connections carry this person in the chat.

PeerLinkState.description: A peer link's state, folded for older apps (`state`): read `link` for the whole of it.

oneOf.description: Not reached yet, this run or a saved one.
The handshake finished and the peer answers.
The WebSocket is open and the handshake runs, or a ping went unanswered.
Down after it was reached (or restarting); its last-known sessions stay listed.

Never reached and attempts failed, the peer refused this daemon's token, or removed
(`error: "removed"`, its last note).

PeerStateChanged.description:
`_acpmux/peer_state_changed`, to every watching connection (`_acpmux/watch`) when a peer's
link changes (`link`, `carrier`, `cause` or `nextRetryAt`), never twice for the same one: a
peer that is added sends its first state, and one that is removed a last `offline` with
`error: "removed"`. Listed as the `peerStateEvents` feature.

at.description: When the note was made, ms since the epoch.

carrier.description: The carrier the open link runs over; null while none is open.

cause.description: Why the link is down; null while it is up or on its way the first time.

error.description: Why the link is down, when it is.

lastSeen.description: The last frame from the peer, ms since the epoch.

link.description: The link's whole state: what a surface draws.

nextRetryAt.description: When acpmux dials again on its own, ms since the epoch; null while it is not waiting.

since.description: When `link` took its value, ms since the epoch.

state.description: `link` folded to the older five words, for an app that predates `link`.

PermissionGroup.description: A batch of permission requests from one turn, decided together.

decision.description: The decision taken, once one was.

decisions.description:
What a respond may choose: all three, or `deny` alone when a pending
item has no single allow-once option.

allowRefused.description:
Set when this reader's group allows would be refused, with the
refusal's reason (`permission.person_required`: only the person
allows a group, and a peer's link never is one). A deny still counts.

macAllowOnce.description:
Set (true) beside `allowRefused` when this daemon still counts a group's
one-time allow signed by an enrolled Mac for every pending member
(`_meta.acpmux.approverDecisions`, `hub/mac_approvers.rs`).

replayed.description: An earlier respond with the same key and body answered this.

decisionKey.description: 1 to 256 bytes; the same key with the same body replays the receipt.

revision.description: The group revision the decision was made on.

groupId.description: One group; absent lists them all. Never null.

PermissionPending.description:
To attached clients (and watchers not attached) when a permission or
question waits: the log record's message (the agent's request with
acpmux's `permissionId`) plus where it came from.

decisionNonce.description: Signs an allow relayed for the person (`hub/person.rs`).

groupId.description: The batch it joined, if any.

annotations.description: Claude Code AskUserQuestion annotations beside the answers, by question text: `{preview?, notes?}`.

optionId.description: The option chosen; absent cancels the request.

PersonHold.description:
What a daemon start holds for a person (`SessionSummary::person_hold`): the chat's folder and
why an agent does not start there unasked.

PresenceNote.description:
`_acpmux/presence`, to every connection attached to the chat on each change, and
`presence` in the `_acpmux/attach` reply. Never in the log, `_acpmux/events` or an export.

participants.description: One per person, by id; at most 32 besides the owner.

ProcessBackgroundParams.description:
`_acpmux/process/background` (Ctrl-B): the chat whose running work goes
to the background, and the one tool call to move (none: every
foreground task, as Claude Code's own Ctrl-B does).

sessionId.description: The chat's id, name or unique prefix.

toolCallId.description: Only the task this tool call started.

backgrounded.description:
Claude Code moved something: the tasks arrive as `process_update`s
with origin `user_backgrounded`. False when nothing ran in the
foreground (or no turn ran).

PromptClass.description: What another agent's message asks of the session it goes to.

oneOf.description: The sender cannot go on until the receiver acts.
The sender asks something and waits for the answer.
The sender reports work it finished. A message sent with no class is one.
Information to read at leisure.

PurgedSession.description: A purged session: only its id is left.

QueuedAuthor.description: The person who queued a prompt in a shared chat.

avatar.description:
Their profile picture (`_meta.provenance` `fromAvatar`, an `https://` URL), left out when
they have none (and from an older acpmux).

QueuedImage.description: An image a queued prompt sends.

id.description:
The SHA-256 of its bytes (64 lowercase hex digits): `_acpmux/attachment {sessionId, id}`
reads it, and `_acpmux/queue_edit` `update` `images` keeps it.

name.description: Its file name, when the client gave one.

source.description: The app it came from (`{name, bundleId?, site?}`), as the prompt's display metadata named it. Absent otherwise.

QueuedPromptSummary.description: A prompt waiting for the running turn to end.

author.description:
The teammate who queued it in a shared chat (`_meta.provenance` `person_message`,
`author.rs`), null for the owner's and for an agent's message: an app shows it under their
name and offers none of its own actions on it (only they change it, `queue.not_author`).
Kept across a restart and by their own edit.

awaitingOwner.description:
A person's prompt that waits for the chat's owner (`author.approval: "owner"`): the queue
runs past it until the owner approves it (`_acpmux/queue_approve`, naming `turnId` and `revision`) or
declines it (`_acpmux/queue_decline`). The owner's pane draws Approve and Decline on it.

class.description:
What another agent's message asks of this chat (`_meta.acpmux.class`, `prompt_class.rs`):
`result` when it named none; null for the person's own prompt and from a peer on an older
acpmux.

fromAgent.description:
The sending agent's name when it is another agent's message, null for the person's: an
app draws it as a received message waiting for the turn, not as a composer row.

fromHarness.description:
That session's harness family (`claude`, `codex`, ...), bound the same way: what an app
draws the sender's icon from. Null when unknown (a mesh relay carries none yet).

fromSessionId.description:
The sending session's id when the daemon bound it (its caller token, a peer daemon's word
on its own proven caller, the mesh relay's sender, a lane's report), null otherwise
(`prompt_provenance.rs` `FROM_SESSION_ID`). Display only, never authority.

held.description: Waits behind a failed turn until the queue is resumed.

heldByStop.description:
Another agent's message the person's Stop holds (`hub/cancel.rs`): it waits until the
person's next turn completes or the queue is resumed. False otherwise; absent from a peer
on an older acpmux.

images.description: The images it sends, in its order; `_acpmux/attachment` reads each by its id.

inboxNotice.description:
acpmux's inbox notice of other agents' messages (`_meta.provenance` `inbox_notice`,
`hub/inbox.rs`): that provenance, `{kind, noticeId, threads}`, so an app draws it as the
messages it carries and never as the person's queued prompt, also when it has not read
its `queued` record (a chat reopened on a recent page). Null for any other prompt, and
once edited (an edit drops the provenance).

provenance.description:
Its `_meta.provenance` when it names a sender that is no agent's to act on: another agent's
message the person edited (`editedBy`, still that agent's words to read) or a prompt no
proof attributes (`unverified`). An app draws its card from it while `fromAgent` is null.
Null otherwise. Display only, never authority.

revision.description: Its version for the owner's approval: 0 when queued, one more at each edit by its author.

subagentRetry.description:
acpmux's own ask that the chat's agent resume a subagent that failed on a transient error
(`_meta.provenance` `subagent_retry`, `hub/subagent_retry.rs`): an app draws it as that
subagent's resume, not as the person's prompt. Null for any other prompt, and once edited
(an edit drops the provenance).

QueuedSubagentRetry.description: The subagent a queued resume asks the agent to resume (`QueuedPromptSummary.subagentRetry`).

agentId.description: The Agent tool's id for it, which the agent resumes it by.

error.description: The transient error it failed on.

name.description: Its task or name, when acpmux knew one.

cmuxGesture.description:
The app's gesture ticket for this exact pick (`transport.gesture`);
the app's relay reads it, acpmux does not.

RetryKind.description: What `_acpmux/retry` retried: the chat's own turn, or one of its subagents.

RetryParams.description:
`_acpmux/retry` (the Retry button, `acpmux retry`): retry the chat's failed last turn now,
in the same session (`hub/auto_resume/retry_turn.rs`).

sessionId.description: The chat's id, name or unique prefix.

subagentId.description:
One of the chat's failed subagents to resume instead, by its id or agent id
(`hub/subagent_retry_manual.rs`), never taken as the chat's own turn.

RetryReason.description:
Why a turn is retried (`hub::turn_errors::resume_cause`): the provider or the gateway had no
capacity (HTTP 503 or 529, overloaded, no account free), the connection dropped, the
agent process died mid-turn, or the chat outgrew its model's context window (`context`: it
is compacted, then continued at once).

RetryResult.description:
What `_acpmux/retry` sent: the prompt `promptId` (for the chat's turn `P~resume-n`, the next
attempt of the failed prompt; for a subagent `subagent-retry-<tool>-<attempt>-<ms>`) and the turn
it started.

RetrySummary.description:
An automatic retry of a failed turn that waits (`hub/auto_resume.rs`): attempt `attempt`
of `of`, at `nextAt` (epoch ms). It sends the prompt `promptId~resume-<attempt>` in the same
session, for the cut turn `turnId`.

SessionAuthLogin.description:
`terminal`: run `command` in a terminal on `host` (null: this machine). `route`: edit or
sign in again to the route `routeId`.

SessionAuthParams.description:
A chat by `sessionId`, or by `target` before it has a session (a new tab before its first
send). Exactly one of the two. `refresh`: probe the route and run the harness's own sign-in
check that reads no keychain, when no newer evidence answers.

SessionAuthResult.description:
What `_acpmux/session/auth` answers. A client blocks a send only on `signedOut`, `expired`
or `routeAuthNeeded`; `unknown` never blocks.

detail.description: One sentence: the probe's status, the turn's error, or the check that ran.

evidenceAt.description: When the evidence was observed (ms since the epoch); null when `source` is `none`.

fromSessionId.description:
The chat whose turn is the evidence (`source` `turn`): for a `target`, a chat on this
daemon with the same harness, account home and route.

host.description: The peer the chat runs on; null on this daemon.

login.description: How to sign in: only for `signedOut`, `expired` and `routeAuthNeeded`.

routeId.description: The route the chat is bound to; null when it is not routed.

SessionAuthTarget.description:
The chat a send would start: its harness, the peer it runs on (`host`, a peer name; absent:
this daemon) and the route the picker selected (absent: the harness's default route, as at
spawn).

cwd.description: Absolute project directory on the destination daemon. Absent: project auth is unknown.

SessionChanged.description:
To watchers when a session changed: its new summary (only its id when
purged), the coarse `kind` and the log record behind it.

peer.description: The peer a remote session runs on.

SessionDetail.description:
A session as `_acpmux/attach` returns it: its summary plus what an
attached client draws (`Hub::session_detail`).

backgroundsWork.description:
`_acpmux/process/background` (Ctrl-B) moves its foreground work: its
harness is Claude Code (claude-stdio), whatever the harness's name.
Clients offer Ctrl-B from this, not from `harness`.

children.description: Its sub-sessions that are not closed.

createdBy.description:
Who created it (`hub/created_by.rs`): `{kind: "person"|"agent"|"script", workspace?,
session?}`, decided by the daemon from the connection, never from a request value.
Null for a fork, a moved-in session and one saved before it existed; absent from a
peer on an older acpmux.

cwd.description: Lossy when the path is not UTF-8.

depth.description:
Its lineage depth (`parent`): 0 for a root session, 1 for the sessions
its agent started, and so on.

effort.description:
The harness's current reasoning effort, when it reports one.
Additive for older clients and peers.

forkSeq.description: Where a fork branched off its parent.

harnessSandboxFailed.description:
Unix milliseconds when its harness first refused a command because the harness's own
sandbox did not start (`hub/harness_sandbox.rs`). Omitted for peers.

harnessSandboxFailing.description:
Whether its harness refuses commands now for that reason; a completed command or a new
harness process ends it (`hub/harness_sandbox.rs`). Omitted for peers.

indicator.description: The status dot every client draws (`status_indicator`); null for none.

inputSince.description: Since when it waits on the person (`lane`); null while it does not.

lane.description: What it is doing and since when (`views::lane`); null for a closed session.

lastMessage.description: One sidebar line; null before the first prompt.

lastReturn.description:
The person's return to the chat while they stay on it (`hub/seen.rs`): `since` and the
`turns` that ended unseen. A client opening the chat then draws "New since you looked" at
`since`, also when its attach answers before its list read.

lifecycleReceipt.description:
An optional controller/daemon lifecycle receipt. It is absent until a
producer supplies a validated receipt; clients must not infer one from
status or placement fields.

loopEpisode.description:
A live repeated-tool episode (`hub/loop_detector.rs`), if this turn is looping.
Additive so older clients and peers can omit it.

mcpServers.description:
The MCP servers the harness says it loaded, from its own report (Claude
Code's system/init); null when it reports none (every ACP harness).

movedTo.description:
Moved to another daemon (`acpmux session move`): where it runs now,
`{host?, sessionId, cwd?, branch?, commit?}`. It never runs here again. Absent otherwise,
and from a peer on an older acpmux.

moving.description: Being moved to another daemon; it takes no prompt meanwhile.

nameGiven.description:
Someone gave `name` (at the start, a fork's or a rename), not the daemon's `HARNESS-N`
default. Absent otherwise, from a session named before it was kept, and from a peer on an
older acpmux.

parent.description:
The session whose agent started this one (`acpmux new` in its shell, or its
`start_session` tool), recorded at creation from the proven caller; null for a
session a person or the app started. Not the fork parent (`parentId`). Absent
from a peer on an older acpmux.

peer.description: The peer daemon a remote session runs on; absent for this daemon's own.

pending.description: Permission requests waiting for an answer.

personHold.description:
A daemon start holds what this chat queued until a person opens it: its folder is guarded
(`hub/protected_hold.rs`). `session resume` names it and NOW says why the queue does not
drain. Absent otherwise, and from a peer on an older acpmux.

pullRequests.description:
The pull request URLs its `gh pr create` calls printed, oldest first;
absent from a peer on an older acpmux.

queuePaused.description: A turn failed: the prompts behind it wait for a client to resume them.

retiredAgentSessionIds.description:
The chat's earlier native ids, oldest first (`SessionMeta::retired_agent_session_ids`):
a Codex chat's earlier roots, which its older records still name, so a client folding
them never reads one as a subagent. Absent when none, and from a peer on an older acpmux.

retry.description:
The automatic retry of its failed last turn that waits (`hub/auto_resume.rs`); null
when none waits.

retryDeciding.description:
Its last turn failed on an error an automatic retry answers, and whether, and when, it
is retried is not settled yet: `retry` is about to be set or stay null, or the retry is
starting or runs (`hub/auto_resume.rs`). `_acpmux/wait` answers for that turn once it is
settled. Absent otherwise, and from a peer on an older acpmux.

root.description:
The root of its lineage tree: the first ancestor no agent started; its own
id for a root. Absent from a peer on an older acpmux.

rules.description: The session has its own permission rules.

seenSeq.description:
The log seq the person had seen when they last stopped showing the chat: a client
opening it while `unreadTurns` is above 0 draws "New since you looked" after it.

shortName.description: Its name among its parent's sub-sessions; null for a root.

shown.description: Some attached client shows the chat.

spawnToolCallId.description: The parent's tool call that started it, when acpmux could tell.

spawnedBy.description:
The session whose agent started this one, kept only while that parent
is listed and is a root itself: one level, for lists that fold one level.
`parent` without those rules, else an older client's `spawnedBy` tag.

startedBy.description:
The session whose agent started this one with its `start_session`
tool (`hub/subsessions.rs`); null for a session a person or client
started. Kept when the parent is closed or gone, so a client draws
the tree from these links at any depth.

starting.description:
Its agent is being started (a start, a wake or a mode change holds the session's spawn
lease, as `stop --if-idle` reads it): a daemon restart now ends that start, so an update
waits on it as on a turn. Always sent, so a row without it is from an older acpmux,
which an update reads by its row's age instead.

state.description: Effective liveness: `stopping` while a Stop waits for its turn to end, `stuck` after three classified harness failures, else `status`.

steering.description: The agent takes a prompt mid-turn.

stuckError.description: Last classified error, redacted and bounded. Omitted for peers.

stuckSince.description: Unix milliseconds when the third failure established stuck. Omitted for peers.

timeBreakdown.description:
Incremental wall-time and token attribution for the chat. This is seeded by a detail or
attach read and omitted from census rows until then (`hub/time_breakdown.rs`).

titleSource.description:
Who supplied `title`: `prompt` is the first-prompt fallback, while
`harness`, `generated` and `adopted` are real chat titles. Older peers
may omit this field.

tools.description: The chat's tools (`hub/tools.rs`), present on per-session reads and attachments.

toolsMutable.description: `_acpmux/set_tools` can change them; omitted from census rows.

transcriptSeq.description:
The seq of its newest transcript record (`hub/paging.rs` `is_transcript`): unlike
`updatedAt` and `lastSeq`, bookkeeping (an agent start's `agent_start_waiting`, usage,
git, process counts) never moves it, so a client that keeps a chat's newest page reads it
again only when this passes the value it read at. An upper bound after a hard stop.
Absent from a peer on an older acpmux.

unreadTurns.description:
Turns that ended while no client showed the chat, since a person last showed it
(`hub/seen.rs`): the sidebar's count. Absent from a peer on an older acpmux.

usageStats.description:
What its harness spends and holds, from the harness's own records
(`usage_stats.rs`); absent until a Claude Code or Codex chat's records
are found, for any other harness, and from a peer on an older acpmux.

waitingOn.description:
What it waits on the person for: `question` (an agent question) or
`permission`; null while nothing is pending. Only the person allows a permission.

waitingPrompt.description: The first prompt of the question it waits on, cut to 120 characters.

waitsForSlot.description:
A sub-session whose queued prompt waits for a free run slot of its parent: the parent
runs as many sub-sessions as its `maxRunning` allows (`hub/subsession_runs.rs`). Absent
otherwise, and from a peer on an older acpmux.

watching.description: The family of a conversation another app runs that this chat only shows; null otherwise.

SessionEvent.description: One record of a session's log (`server::event_value`).

dir.description:
`in` (agent to acpmux), `out` (acpmux to agent), `mux` (acpmux's own)
or `peer`.

kind.description:
The JSON-RPC method, the `sessionUpdate` value, or an acpmux kind such
as `status`.

msg.description: The raw JSON-RPC message, or acpmux's payload.

SessionSummary.description:
One session as every list shows it (`Hub::session_summary`). A peer's
session arrives as the peer daemon's own summary plus `peer`, with
`status` `unreachable` while the peer is gone; a peer on an older
acpmux may lack newer fields, so nullable ones are optional here.

backgroundsWork.description:
`_acpmux/process/background` (Ctrl-B) moves its foreground work: its
harness is Claude Code (claude-stdio), whatever the harness's name.
Clients offer Ctrl-B from this, not from `harness`.

children.description: Its sub-sessions that are not closed.

createdBy.description:
Who created it (`hub/created_by.rs`): `{kind: "person"|"agent"|"script", workspace?,
session?}`, decided by the daemon from the connection, never from a request value.
Null for a fork, a moved-in session and one saved before it existed; absent from a
peer on an older acpmux.

cwd.description: Lossy when the path is not UTF-8.

depth.description:
Its lineage depth (`parent`): 0 for a root session, 1 for the sessions
its agent started, and so on.

effort.description:
The harness's current reasoning effort, when it reports one.
Additive for older clients and peers.

forkSeq.description: Where a fork branched off its parent.

harnessSandboxFailed.description:
Unix milliseconds when its harness first refused a command because the harness's own
sandbox did not start (`hub/harness_sandbox.rs`). Omitted for peers.

harnessSandboxFailing.description:
Whether its harness refuses commands now for that reason; a completed command or a new
harness process ends it (`hub/harness_sandbox.rs`). Omitted for peers.

indicator.description: The status dot every client draws (`status_indicator`); null for none.

inputSince.description: Since when it waits on the person (`lane`); null while it does not.

lane.description: What it is doing and since when (`views::lane`); null for a closed session.

lastMessage.description: One sidebar line; null before the first prompt.

lastReturn.description:
The person's return to the chat while they stay on it (`hub/seen.rs`): `since` and the
`turns` that ended unseen. A client opening the chat then draws "New since you looked" at
`since`, also when its attach answers before its list read.

lifecycleReceipt.description:
An optional controller/daemon lifecycle receipt. It is absent until a
producer supplies a validated receipt; clients must not infer one from
status or placement fields.

loopEpisode.description:
A live repeated-tool episode (`hub/loop_detector.rs`), if this turn is looping.
Additive so older clients and peers can omit it.

mcpServers.description:
The MCP servers the harness says it loaded, from its own report (Claude
Code's system/init); null when it reports none (every ACP harness).

movedTo.description:
Moved to another daemon (`acpmux session move`): where it runs now,
`{host?, sessionId, cwd?, branch?, commit?}`. It never runs here again. Absent otherwise,
and from a peer on an older acpmux.

moving.description: Being moved to another daemon; it takes no prompt meanwhile.

nameGiven.description:
Someone gave `name` (at the start, a fork's or a rename), not the daemon's `HARNESS-N`
default. Absent otherwise, from a session named before it was kept, and from a peer on an
older acpmux.

parent.description:
The session whose agent started this one (`acpmux new` in its shell, or its
`start_session` tool), recorded at creation from the proven caller; null for a
session a person or the app started. Not the fork parent (`parentId`). Absent
from a peer on an older acpmux.

peer.description: The peer daemon a remote session runs on; absent for this daemon's own.

personHold.description:
A daemon start holds what this chat queued until a person opens it: its folder is guarded
(`hub/protected_hold.rs`). `session resume` names it and NOW says why the queue does not
drain. Absent otherwise, and from a peer on an older acpmux.

pullRequests.description:
The pull request URLs its `gh pr create` calls printed, oldest first;
absent from a peer on an older acpmux.

queuePaused.description: A turn failed: the prompts behind it wait for a client to resume them.

retiredAgentSessionIds.description:
The chat's earlier native ids, oldest first (`SessionMeta::retired_agent_session_ids`):
a Codex chat's earlier roots, which its older records still name, so a client folding
them never reads one as a subagent. Absent when none, and from a peer on an older acpmux.

retry.description:
The automatic retry of its failed last turn that waits (`hub/auto_resume.rs`); null
when none waits.

retryDeciding.description:
Its last turn failed on an error an automatic retry answers, and whether, and when, it
is retried is not settled yet: `retry` is about to be set or stay null, or the retry is
starting or runs (`hub/auto_resume.rs`). `_acpmux/wait` answers for that turn once it is
settled. Absent otherwise, and from a peer on an older acpmux.

root.description:
The root of its lineage tree: the first ancestor no agent started; its own
id for a root. Absent from a peer on an older acpmux.

rules.description: The session has its own permission rules.

seenSeq.description:
The log seq the person had seen when they last stopped showing the chat: a client
opening it while `unreadTurns` is above 0 draws "New since you looked" after it.

shortName.description: Its name among its parent's sub-sessions; null for a root.

shown.description: Some attached client shows the chat.

spawnToolCallId.description: The parent's tool call that started it, when acpmux could tell.

spawnedBy.description:
The session whose agent started this one, kept only while that parent
is listed and is a root itself: one level, for lists that fold one level.
`parent` without those rules, else an older client's `spawnedBy` tag.

startedBy.description:
The session whose agent started this one with its `start_session`
tool (`hub/subsessions.rs`); null for a session a person or client
started. Kept when the parent is closed or gone, so a client draws
the tree from these links at any depth.

starting.description:
Its agent is being started (a start, a wake or a mode change holds the session's spawn
lease, as `stop --if-idle` reads it): a daemon restart now ends that start, so an update
waits on it as on a turn. Always sent, so a row without it is from an older acpmux,
which an update reads by its row's age instead.

state.description: Effective liveness: `stopping` while a Stop waits for its turn to end, `stuck` after three classified harness failures, else `status`.

steering.description: The agent takes a prompt mid-turn.

stuckError.description: Last classified error, redacted and bounded. Omitted for peers.

stuckSince.description: Unix milliseconds when the third failure established stuck. Omitted for peers.

timeBreakdown.description:
Incremental wall-time and token attribution for the chat. This is seeded by a detail or
attach read and omitted from census rows until then (`hub/time_breakdown.rs`).

titleSource.description:
Who supplied `title`: `prompt` is the first-prompt fallback, while
`harness`, `generated` and `adopted` are real chat titles. Older peers
may omit this field.

tools.description: The chat's tools (`hub/tools.rs`), present on per-session reads and attachments.

toolsMutable.description: `_acpmux/set_tools` can change them; omitted from census rows.

The seq of its newest transcript record (`hub/paging.rs` `is_transcript`): unlike
`updatedAt` and `lastSeq`, bookkeeping (an agent start's `agent_start_waiting`, usage,
git, process counts) never moves it, so a client that keeps a chat's newest page reads it
again only when this passes the value it read at. An upper bound after a hard stop.
Absent from a peer on an older acpmux.

unreadTurns.description:
Turns that ended while no client showed the chat, since a person last showed it
(`hub/seen.rs`): the sidebar's count. Absent from a peer on an older acpmux.

usageStats.description:
What its harness spends and holds, from the harness's own records
(`usage_stats.rs`); absent until a Claude Code or Codex chat's records
are found, for any other harness, and from a peer on an older acpmux.

waitingOn.description:
What it waits on the person for: `question` (an agent question) or
`permission`; null while nothing is pending. Only the person allows a permission.

waitingPrompt.description: The first prompt of the question it waits on, cut to 120 characters.

waitsForSlot.description:
A sub-session whose queued prompt waits for a free run slot of its parent: the parent
runs as many sub-sessions as its `maxRunning` allows (`hub/subsession_runs.rs`). Absent
otherwise, and from a peer on an older acpmux.

watching.description: The family of a conversation another app runs that this chat only shows; null otherwise.

cursor.description: A previous reply's `nextCursor`: the page starts after that session.

excludeStatus.description: `_acpmux/sessions` only: exclude these statuses before pagination.

limit.description: Page size, at least 1. Without it the reply is the whole list.

localOnly.description: `_acpmux/sessions` only: exclude peer sessions before pagination.

orderBy.description: `_acpmux/sessions` only: `sessionId` orders by immutable ID for complete scans.

peer.description:
`_acpmux/sessions` only (a watch refuses it): only the sessions this acpmux peer owns
(its name, e.g. `huge-blue`). Empty is no filter.

pendingOnly.description:
`_acpmux/sessions` only (a watch refuses it): only the sessions with a pending permission
or question, local and peer, summarized alone and answered without the list's pace.
Takes no other filter; the reply is never paged (capability `session-list-pending-v1`).

status.description:
`_acpmux/sessions` only (a watch refuses it): only the sessions in this status
(`running`, `ready`, `idle`, `waiting`, `closed`). Empty is no filter.

usage.description:
`_acpmux/sessions` only: read each chat's usage from its harness's records first
(`usageStats`; at most one read every 5 s, waited for at most 750 ms). Without it the
rows carry what the last read found.

withTools.description: Include tool inventories explicitly; default census rows omit them.

delta.description:
A watch that sent `known` (`watch_delta.rs`): `sessions` holds only the rows new or
changed since, and the rest of the known rows stand.

nextCursor.description:
With `limit`: the cursor for the next page, null when the list is
done. Absent without `limit`.

removed.description: With `delta`: the known sessions no longer listed.

sessions.description: Local and peer sessions, newest first, then by `sessionId`.

unchanged.description: With `delta`: how many listed rows were left out as unchanged.

turnTokens.description: Whole-turn usage, not usage attributed to this interval.

ToolSummary.description: One row of a chat's tool list (`store::ToolRow`).

canToggle.description: `_acpmux/set_tools` can turn it on or off in this chat.

source.description: What gives it: `cmux`, or the harness that reported it (`claude`).

activity.description:
What the turn does right now: its latest tool call's title, masked
(`secret_scan`); null until it calls one (`hub/activity.rs`).

planStep.description: Its plan's entry in progress, masked; null without one.

TypingParams.description:
`_acpmux/typing`: at most 2 a second per connection (`typing.rate_limited`); an `on`
lapses after 8 s. The connection must be attached to the chat.

UsageStats.description:
A chat's spend and context as its harness recorded them (`usage_stats.rs`):
Claude Code's transcript and its subagents' (their spend is the chat's), or
Codex's rollout. Read from where the last read ended: by a session list
that asks (`usage: true`) or an info read, at most every 5 s, and by each
turn's end for its own chat, recorded then as a mux `usage_stats` record.
A value that could not be read is null, never 0: a count is null while
the reads have not covered the whole last day (a first read cut short
before it, a backlog not read yet, a file that could not be read).

autocompact.description: Whether something caps the context at which the harness compacts.

autocompactCap.description:
The cap, when `autocompact` is `capped` and its value is known (Claude
Code's `--autocompact`, `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW`,
`CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE` of a known window, `autoCompactWindow`;
Codex's `model_auto_compact_token_limit`); null otherwise.

cacheReadShare24h.description:
Of those calls' prompt tokens (input, cache read and cache write), the share the prompt
cache served (0 to 1); null with no calls or when the day is not read whole.

calls24h.description: Model calls of the last 24 hours, subagents' included.

contextTokens.description: The last call's context: its input, cache read and cache write tokens.

contextWindow.description: The model's context window, as the harness reported it, else the catalog's.

costPerCallUsd24h.description: `costUsd24h` over the priced calls: what one call costs at list prices, USD.

costUsd24h.description:
Those tokens at the model catalog's list prices, USD; null when no model
they ran on has a price, or when `tokens24h` is null.

launcher.description:
The executable its harness runs, by file name (`claude`, `claude-sr2`,
`codex-acp`); `harness` is the profile. Null when this daemon did not
start it (an adopted, watched or revived chat).

subagents1h.description: Subagents started in the last hour.

subagents24h.description: Subagents started in the last 24 hours.

tokens24h.description:
Tokens of the last 24 hours, subagents' included: input, output, cache
read and cache write.

updatedAt.description: Unix ms of the read these come from.

_meta.description:
An author changes only that person's presence (`hub/presence.rs`), not whether the
chat counts as shown.

visible.description: The attached client shows the chat (`hub/seen.rs`).

enabled.description:
Default true: every session's changes arrive as
`_acpmux/session_changed`.

known.description:
A peer daemon's link only (`watch_delta.rs`): every session it holds of this daemon's
list, with the digest of its row as last listed (`""` when it changed since). The reply
is then a delta: `delta: true`, the rows new or changed, and `removed`.

withTools.description: Include tool inventories explicitly; default census rows omit them.
